column1: # The position table of targets/xkb.md (rule keyName): the default XKB key name per position name, with the keycode
# it has in xkeyboard-config's evdev keycodes, the aliases those keycodes define for it, and the navigation keysym of
# the number-pad keys (rule keyType, numLock positions).
# Sources (read 2026-11-28; names and values only, see CLEAN-ROOM.md "Linux (XKB) sources"):
#   chromium = Chromium ui/events/keycodes/dom/dom_code_data.inc (BSD-3-Clause), its XKB column (X keycode =
#              Linux evdev code + 8) joined by the W3C code value (the position name) of each row:
#   evdev    = the key name that xkeyboard-config's keycodes/evdev (section "evdev") gives that keycode, and the
#              aliases of keycodes/evdev and keycodes/aliases (section "qwerty") that name it; xkeyboard-config
#   keypad   = the first-level keysym of the key in xkeyboard-config's symbols/keypad, section "x11"
# Columns: position, keyName, keycode (X keycode, decimal), aliases ("-" = none), keypad (navigation keysym, "-" =
# none), source. Every Table A position (targets/windows-default-vk.tsv) has a row except SysRq and Break, which
# have no key of their own in XKB: SysRq is the second level of <PRSC> (Alt+Print, keycode 107 = evdev KEY_SYSRQ
# 99 + 8) and Break the second level of <PAUS> (Control+Pause), both in xkeyboard-config's symbols/pc. The
# positions of SPEC Appendix A that Table A lacks (NumpadEqual, KanaMode, IntlRo, Convert, NonConvert, IntlYen,
# NumpadComma) and Lang1, Lang2 are added.
